questions.question:
Which of the following idiom given in the alternatives has the meaning?
Enjoy oneself very much

options.text: Have a nick of a time
Have a click of a time
Have a whale of a time
Have a shell of a time

questions.solution:
The correct answer is '3' i.e. Have a whale of a time .

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The idiom **"Have a whale of a time"** means to enjoy oneself very much or have a great time.
 
• It is often used in informal contexts to describe a fun or exciting experience.

Correct sentence: *We had a whale of a time at the party last night.*

• **Have a nick of a time:** Not a commonly used idiom or phrase.
 
• **Have a click of a time:** Not a recognized idiom in English.
 
• **Have a shell of a time:** Doesn't carry the intended meaning of enjoying oneself.
 
 
 
• **Using idioms:** Idioms are phrases that have figurative meanings, and they are often tied to cultural or linguistic contexts.
</ul

questions.question:
Which of the following options is the most suitable conversion of the following sentence into Passive Voice?

People believed that he was innocent.

options.text: It will believe that he was innocent.
He was believe to be innocent by people.
It was believed that he was innocent.
His innocence was believe by people.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is '3' i.e. It was believed that he was innocent.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The given sentence is in the **active voice**: "People believed that he was innocent."
 
• To convert this sentence into the **passive voice**, the following changes are required:
 
 
• The object of the active sentence ("that he was innocent") becomes the subject of the passive sentence.
 
• The verb "believed" is changed to its passive form "was believed."
 
• The subject of the active sentence ("People") is either omitted (as it's a general reference) or retained in a prepositional phrase starting with "by."
 
 
 
• Therefore, the correct passive voice conversion is: **"It was believed that he was innocent."**

Correct sentence: *It was believed that he was innocent.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Key rules for converting active to passive voice:**

 
 
• The object of the active voice becomes the subject in the passive voice.
 
• The verb is replaced with its corresponding passive form: **be + past participle**.
 
• The subject of the active voice is either omitted (if it's a general reference) or introduced using "by."
 
 
 
• **Example:**
 
 
• Active: "The team completed the project."
 
• Passive: "The project was completed by the team."

questions.question:
Which of the following options is the most suitable conversion of the following sentence into Passive Voice?

Didn't the manager inform all the employees about the new rule?

options.text: Weren't all the employees informed about the new rule by the manager?
Wasn't all the employees informed about the new rule by the manager?
Didn't all the employees informed about the new rule by the manager?
Doesn't all the employees informed about the new rule by the manager?

questions.solution:
The correct answer is '1' i.e. Weren't all the employees informed about the new rule by the manager?

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The given sentence is in the **interrogative** form of the **active voice**, starting with "Didn't."
 
• When converting such sentences into the **passive voice**, the structure becomes: **Wasn't/Weren't + subject (object of active voice) + past participle + by + agent (doer).**
 
• In the active voice, "the manager" is the subject, "all the employees" is the object, and the verb is "inform."
 
• In the passive voice, the object "all the employees" becomes the subject, and the verb changes to the past participle "informed."
 
• Option 1 correctly follows this structure: **Weren't all the employees informed about the new rule by the manager?**

Correct sentence: *Weren't all the employees informed about the new rule by the manager?*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 2:** "Wasn't all the employees informed about the new rule by the manager?" is incorrect because "employees" is plural, so the correct auxiliary verb should be "Weren't," not "Wasn't."
 
• **Option 3:** "Didn't all the employees informed about the new rule by the manager?" is incorrect because "informed" is not used correctly as a past participle in the passive voice.
 
• **Option 4:** "Doesn't all the employees informed about the new rule by the manager?" is incorrect because it mixes present tense ("Doesn't") with past participle "informed," which is grammatically wrong.

questions.question:
Which of the following options is the most suitable conversion of the following sentence into active voice?

You are requested to come early tomorrow.

options.text: I request your early coming tomorrow.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is '3' i.e. Please come early tomorrow.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The given sentence is in the** passive voice**, as it starts with "You are requested," indicating a polite request.
 
• In the active voice, the sentence needs to be rewritten to directly convey the request while maintaining the same meaning.
 
• Option 3, "Please come early tomorrow," is the most appropriate active voice conversion because it is polite and directly conveys the request.
 
• Options 1, 2, and 4 are either grammatically incorrect or do not match the tone and intent of the original sentence.

Correct sentence: *Please come early tomorrow*.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Passive to Active Voice Conversion Tips:**

 
 
• Identify the subject performing the action in the passive sentence.
 
• Rewrite the sentence so that the subject appears at the beginning, performing the action.
 
• Use appropriate verbs and maintain the tone of the original sentence (e.g., polite requests should remain polite).
 
 
 
• **Examples:**
 
 
• Passive: "The homework was completed by the student." → Active: "The student completed the homework."
 
• Passive: "You are advised to take precautions." → Active: "Please take precautions."

• **Existential issues:** Deep mental and philosophical suffering.
 
• **Daily accomplishment:** Problem-solving and functional needs.
 
 
 
• The simultaneous management of all these diverse layers—emotional, relational, practical, and existential—is what makes the process "complicated."
 
• Why other options are incorrect: 
 
 
• **Option 1:** This **contradicts** the text. The passage describes a need for being there "again and again" through various sufferings, which is the opposite of a "one-off" intervention or simple medication.
 
• **Option 3:** The passage explicitly states that care **is** the task of addressing "adverse life circumstances," meaning it must be deeply involved in real-life situations.
 
• **Option 4:** This is a **narrow view** that the passage is trying to move away from by focusing on "dignity," "disability justice," and "existential issues" rather than just a medical diagnosis.
 
 

Therefore, the correct answer is **2**.

 

**Analytical Insight:** *In high-level Reading Comprehension, "Complexity" usually arises from the **intersection** of different factors. When a text lists multiple categories of needs that must be addressed at the same time, the "complication" lies in that holistic approach.*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Existential:** Relating to human existence or the experience of being alive.
 
• **Equity:** The quality of being fair and impartial, ensuring everyone has what they need to succeed.
 
• **Disability Justice:** A movement that acknowledges that all bodies are unique and that social systems must be built to include everyone.
 
• **Adverse:** Preventing success or development; harmful; unfavorable.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 4**.

__
 
• To identify the passage's attitude toward these needs, we look at the final sentence: *"...care as the task of addressing adverse life circumstances... **while at the same time addressing needs related to security, relationship, daily accomplishment, or problem-solving**, is a very complicated story."*
 
• The use of the phrase **"while at the same time"** indicates that these practical and social needs (security, relationships, accomplishment) are not separate from mental health care but are **interconnected** with it.
 
• The "radical vision" described doesn't choose between fixing life circumstances and fixing the mind; it advocates for addressing **both** simultaneously.
 
• **Option 4** perfectly reflects this holistic attitude by stating these needs must be addressed **alongside** emotional and existential suffering.
 
• Why other options are incorrect: 
 
 
• **Option 1:** The passage suggests they should be addressed "at the same time," which is the opposite of considering them "individually" or as "different from mental health."
 
• **Option 2:** This is **too restrictive**. The passage also mentions relationships, daily accomplishment, and problem-solving, not just security.
 
• **Option 3:** This **contradicts** the text, which explicitly includes these needs as part of the "task of care" in its complicated story.
 
 

Therefore, the correct answer is **4**.

 

**Analytical Insight:** *In high-level Reading Comprehension, look for "Integrative" keywords like "while," "simultaneously," or "at the same time." These words signal that the author views various elements as a **unified whole** rather than isolated parts.*

• **Adverse:** Unfavorable or harmful circumstances.
